title: Decoding India's New Income Tax Act: Simpler Rules, Clearer Taxes
description: India has replaced its old Income Tax Act, 1961, with the new Income Tax Act, 2025, from April 1, 2026. The main goal is to simplify tax laws, reduce paperwor.

faq.a: The 'Tax Year' is the new term for the financial year, which runs from April 1 to March 31. It replaces the 'Previous Year' concept, and the 'Assessment Year' concept has been removed.

faq.q: When did this new Act come into effect?
faq.a: The Income Tax Act, 2025, came into effect from April 1, 2026. This means it applies to income earned during the financial year 2026-27 and onwards.

faq.q: Does this new Act change my income tax slabs or rates?
faq.a: No, the new Act's main focus is on simplifying the structure and language of tax laws. It does not introduce new tax slabs or rates, which were largely set out in the Budget 2026.

faq.q: Will I still be able to claim deductions like Section 80C?
faq.a: Yes, if you choose to file under the old tax regime, deductions under sections like 80C, 80D, and others are still available. The new tax regime, while the default, offers fewer deductions.

faq.q: What happens if I make a small mistake in my tax filing under the new rules?
faq.a: The new rules aim to be less harsh on minor errors. For instance, prosecution under the Black Money Act for small foreign asset non-disclosures (up to ₹20 lakh, excluding immovable property) will not apply from October 1, 2024.
